plain_english: This is a Lanark Commissary Court testament, notwithstanding the Edinburgh folder in which the PDF is stored.
The estate includes livestock, crops, household possessions and clothing. The heading states that no debts were owed to the deceased; debts owed by him are then listed.

George Brown and John Neilson appear in the executor-dative administration. The production wording immediately after their names is not securely resolved in this crop. William Neilson in Biggar appears as cautioner.
These are administrative roles. The inspected passages do not securely call any of these men William Glasgow's relative.
The original's opening death-date wording is partly obscured and is not sufficiently secure to replace the maintained before-April-1673 death boundary.
findings: Original images have now been inspected: the former statement that the original had not been reviewed is superseded for this source-review record.

No securely read spouse, parent, child or sibling clause was recovered. The wording after George Brown and John Neilson is procedural but not securely readable as 'particular Inventar'. This is a qualified result of an incomplete transcription, not proof that no such wording exists.
No evidence recovered here links this William to the Cavers/Ulster William or Glasgow-591.
Quothquan is retained from the previously maintained index-based identification; the obscured original locality spelling was not independently resolved here.
